"PROJECT: CHITTAGONG LIFE

Hyper-Realistic Open-World Game

Act as a professional AAA game development studio. Create a GTA-inspired, hyper-realistic 3D open-world game set in Chattogram, Bangladesh.

Technology:

- Unreal Engine 5.
- C++ and Blueprints.
- Android and iOS.
- Third-person gameplay.
- Optimized for mobile devices.

1. GRAPHICS

Create next-generation AAA-quality graphics.

- Photorealistic environments and buildings.
- Realistic human characters and faces.
- Detailed skin, hair and clothing.
- Lumen lighting and Nanite where supported.
- Realistic shadows and reflections.
- Cinematic skies and atmospheric effects.
- Realistic water, vegetation and roads.
- Dynamic weather and rain.

Characters should have subtle anime-inspired aesthetics but realistic human proportions and detailed appearances. Avoid cartoonish graphics.

2. OPEN-WORLD CITY: CHITTAGONG

Recreate five real Chattogram locations with accurate geographical relationships, roads, intersections and recognizable landmarks.

GEC Circle: Commercial area, shopping malls, restaurants and busy intersections.

Chawkbazar: Traditional markets, narrow streets, mosques and crowded local shops.

Agrabad: Modern skyscrapers, corporate offices, banks and business centers.

Muradpur: Residential buildings, apartments, schools and local businesses.

Patenga: Beautiful beaches, lighthouse, ocean, coastal roads and restaurants.

GOOGLE MAPS REFERENCES

GEC Circle:
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1@COMMENT_BODY@query=GEC+Circle+Chattogram

Chawkbazar:
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1@COMMENT_BODY@query=Chawkbazar+Chattogram

Agrabad:
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1@COMMENT_BODY@query=Agrabad+Chattogram

Muradpur:
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1@COMMENT_BODY@query=Muradpur+Chattogram

Patenga:
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1@COMMENT_BODY@query=Patenga+Beach+Chattogram

Use these locations as geographical references. Create original 3D buildings and environments inspired by their real-world appearance.

3. CHARACTER SYSTEM

Create a customizable realistic 3D character.

Include:

- Walking, running and sprinting.
- Jumping, climbing and swimming.
- Fighting, dodging and blocking.
- Realistic character animations.
- Different hairstyles and outfits.
- Character customization.

Implement a smooth GTA-style third-person camera with adjustable zoom and rotation.

4. VEHICLES

Include:

- Sports cars.
- Sedans and SUVs.
- Motorcycles.
- Buses and trucks.
- CNG auto-rickshaws.
- Traditional rickshaws.

Implement realistic driving physics, vehicle damage, headlights, horns, garages, parking and vehicle customization.

Create intelligent traffic AI with realistic Bangladeshi traffic behaviour.

5. NPC AND CITY LIFE

Create an interactive living city containing pedestrians, students, shopkeepers, businessmen, drivers, tourists and police.

NPCs should walk, talk, shop, work, drive and interact naturally.

Implement daily routines, realistic crowd density and district-specific behaviours.

IMPORTANT: This is PART 1 of the project instructions. Do not start full development yet. Wait for PART 2 before finalizing the complete game architecture. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Build a playable Chittagong Life open-world game prototype set in Chattogram, Bangladesh.

## Requirements
- User described a third-person mobile game with five Chattogram districts, exploration, customizable character, vehicles, NPCs, weather, and realistic city atmosphere.
- User also said this was “PART 1” and to wait for PART 2 before finalizing the complete game architecture, while also requesting a playable game now.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js prototype rather than an Unreal Engine project, using original procedural city geometry and mobile-friendly controls.
- Focused this first playable build on walking/driving exploration, five district landmarks, a city guide, weather, and ambient audio; it does not implement the full AAA feature list.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a playable 3D Chattogram city prototype with five districts, district-specific architecture, roads, coastal water, pedestrians, vehicles, day clock, weather cycling, and landmark discovery.
- Added third-person camera controls, keyboard/touch movement, hop, vehicle interaction, responsive HUD, and a full city map.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser opened at `http://localhost:3002`; screenshot saved and inspected at `screenshots/chittagong.jpg`.

### Active
- Awaiting any further project instructions, including the referenced PART 2, before finalizing full game architecture.

### Blocked
- None. The browser console had a non-game 404 for `/favicon.ico`; WebGL performance warnings appeared under software rendering.

## Next Move
1. If the user supplies PART 2, incorporate it before finalizing architecture.
2. Otherwise, report the current browser prototype and its scope, noting that it is not an Unreal Engine 5 production game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game HUD and page structure.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, gameplay, controls, interactions, and systems.
- `style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile interface and touch controls.
- `screenshots/chittagong.jpg`: Latest browser screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- The prototype loads Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Development server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002` in tmux session `chittagong-dev`.

content.text:
## Chittagong Life prototype is ready

I built a playable browser-based 3D prototype with five distinct Chattogram neighborhoods, landmarks, pedestrians, traffic, CNGs and rickshaws, a city guide, weather changes, and desktop/mobile controls.

**Play it:** [http://localhost:3002](http://localhost:3002)  
**Controls:** WASD or the mobile joystick to move; Shift or RUN to sprint; Space to hop; E or TALK / VIEW to interact; drag to rotate the camera; use the map and weather buttons to explore.

I validated `game.js` with `node --check` and opened the game in a browser. The implementation uses Three.js rather than Unreal Engine 5, and the districts are original approximations—not geographically verified recreations. This is a playable first prototype, not a production-ready AAA mobile game; I’m leaving the full architecture open for the referenced Part 2.

CHITTAGONG LIFE – PART 2

Gameplay Systems & Development


Continue the CHITTAGONG LIFE project using all specifications from PART 1.


6. BUSINESS EMPIRE SYSTEM


Allow players to purchase, own and manage:


- Restaurants.
- Clothing stores.
- Shopping malls.
- Hotels.
- Cafes.
- Corporate offices.
- Apartments.
- Beach resorts.


Implement:


- Employee hiring and salaries.
- Inventory management.
- Customer satisfaction.
- Business upgrades.
- Daily income and expenses.
- Profit tracking.
- Property ownership.
- Business expansion.


Allow players to build an entire business empire across Chattogram.


7. MISSIONS AND ACTIVITIES


Create:


- Main story missions.
- Delivery jobs.
- Street racing.
- Business challenges.
- Exploration missions.
- Social interactions.
- Combat missions.
- Side activities.


Players must be able to freely explore without completing missions.


8. INTERIORS


Make selected buildings enterable, including apartments, shops, restaurants, offices, hotels and cafes.


Add interactive doors, furniture, computers, elevators and other objects.


9. WORLD SYSTEMS


Implement:


- Complete 24-hour day/night cycle.
- Dynamic weather and realistic rain.
- Fog and changing atmospheric conditions.
- Realistic traffic and environmental sounds.
- Ocean waves and water physics.
- Police and wanted system.
- Inventory and smartphone.
- GPS and navigation.
- Property ownership.
- Save/load system.


10. UI AND MAP


Create a premium, minimalist GTA-inspired mobile interface.


Include:


- Virtual joystick.
- Jump and sprint buttons.
- Attack and interaction buttons.
- Mini-map and GPS.
- Full interactive city map.
- Inventory.
- Smartphone.
- Business management.
- Vehicle selection.


Create a beautiful aerial 3D city map showing all five districts with selectable locations, district previews and navigation markers.


11. MOBILE OPTIMIZATION


Optimize for Android and iOS.


Target:


- Stable 30 FPS on mid-range devices.
- 60 FPS on capable devices.
- Adjustable graphics settings.
- Low memory usage.
- Fast loading.


Use LOD, world streaming, object pooling, texture compression, NPC distance culling and efficient lighting.


12. DEVELOPMENT PLAN


Build the game in these stages:


1. Character controller and camera.
2. Muradpur as the first playable district.
3. Roads, buildings and environment.
4. NPCs and traffic.
5. Vehicle system.
6. Business and property system.
7. Missions and combat.
8. Remaining four districts.
9. Interiors and advanced world systems.
10. UI, optimization and Android build.


13. IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT RULES


- Build actual playable systems, not static visual mockups.
- Every button and interaction must work.
- Use modular, maintainable code.
- Never remove existing working features.
- Test every major feature.
- Explain where scripts and assets belong.
- Provide complete functional implementations.
- Prioritize graphics and performance together.
- Do not pretend unfinished features are completed.


FINAL VISION


Create a massive, hyper-realistic GTA-inspired open-world game where players can experience life in Chattogram.


Players should be able to explore realistic city districts, drive vehicles, interact with people, complete missions, fight enemies, purchase properties, start businesses and build their own empire.


The final result should feel like a next-generation open-world game with cinematic graphics and immersive gameplay.


Now combine PART 1 and PART 2 and begin development step by step. Start with a fully playable prototype of Muradpur before expanding the entire city.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue CHITTAGONG LIFE using Parts 1 and 2, starting with a playable Muradpur prototype before expanding the city.

## Requirements
- Combine the Part 1 vision with Part 2 gameplay systems and develop step by step.
- Build actual playable systems, preserve working features, test major features, and clearly distinguish finished from unfinished work.
- Keep the full architecture open to future requirements; do not claim the browser prototype is a finished Unreal Engine 5 game.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js browser prototype as a playable vertical slice; full Unreal Engine 5 production remains outside the current implementation.
- Start the player in Muradpur and add a café business, enterable café interior, optional delivery activity, and locally saved progress as the initial Part 2 systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing five-district city prototype includes exploration, vehicles, pedestrians, landmarks, weather, ambient sound, map, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Added a City Life menu with Business, Jobs, and Pocket tabs in `index.html` and styling in `style.css`.
- Added preliminary Muradpur café ownership, staffing, stock, upgrades, hourly earnings/expenses, delivery job, interior entry/exit, wallet, and localStorage save/load logic in `game.js`.
- Changed the initial player position to Muradpur.

### Active
- Validate and finish the new gameplay systems; the latest edits have not yet been syntax-checked or tested in a browser.
- Continue the Muradpur-first playable prototype, then expand systems and districts incrementally.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js`; fix any errors introduced by the latest edits.
2. Launch the prototype and test menu tabs/actions, café purchase and entry/exit, delivery completion, economy, save/load, and existing movement/map/weather/vehicle interactions.
3. Review the UI on desktop and mobile, then document which Part 2 systems remain unimplemented.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js world, existing gameplay, and newly added Muradpur systems.
- `index.html`: HUD and added City Life panel.
- `style.css`: Existing responsive UI and added panel/interior styles.
- `start.sh`: Existing development startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest observed `git status`.
- The new business, job, interior, and persistence changes were made but not yet verified; do not represent them as tested or complete.
- The prototype still uses Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js`; it is not an Unreal Engine 5 build.

## Objective
- Continue CHITTAGONG LIFE from Parts 1 and 2 as a playable Muradpur-first prototype, adding and validating gameplay systems incrementally.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing features and test major systems; distinguish implemented prototype features from unfinished work.
- Keep the architecture open to future requirements; do not present the browser prototype as a finished Unreal Engine 5 game.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js browser prototype as a vertical slice; Unreal Engine 5 production is out of scope.
- Start in Muradpur with a café business, enterable interior, optional delivery activity, and locally saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a City Life menu with Business, Jobs, and Pocket tabs, wallet display, and save status.
- Added initial café purchase, staffing, restocking, upgrades, hourly economy, delivery activity, interior entry/exit, and localStorage persistence logic.
- Set the starting player location to Muradpur.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate new systems in a browser and fix gameplay or presentation issues.
- Check existing movement, map, weather, and vehicle interactions for regressions; inspect desktop and mobile UI.
- Document implemented versus unfinished Part 2 systems.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Start the prototype and test menu tabs/actions, café purchase and entry/exit, delivery completion, economy, and save/load.
2. Check existing movement, map, weather, and vehicle interactions for regressions; inspect desktop and mobile UI.
3. Document implemented versus unfinished Part 2 systems.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js world, existing gameplay, and new Muradpur systems.
- `index.html`: HUD and City Life panel.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI and panel/interior styles.
- `start.sh`: Development startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest observed `git status`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue CHITTAGONG LIFE as a playable Muradpur-first browser prototype, adding and validating gameplay systems incrementally.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing features and test major systems; distinguish implemented prototype features from unfinished work.
- Keep the architecture open to future requirements; do not present the browser prototype as a finished Unreal Engine 5 game.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js browser prototype as a vertical slice; Unreal Engine 5 production is out of scope.
- Start in Muradpur with a café business, enterable interior, optional delivery activity, and locally saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a City Life menu with Business, Jobs, and Pocket tabs, wallet display, and save status.
- Added café purchase, staffing, restocking, upgrades, hourly economy, delivery activity, interior entry/exit, and localStorage persistence logic.
- Set the starting player location to Muradpur.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started the prototype via the server already running at `http://localhost:3000`; the page renders and the HUD reports Muradpur.

### Active
- Validate menu tabs/actions, café purchase and entry/exit, delivery completion, economy, and save/load.
- Check movement, map, weather, vehicle interactions, and mobile UI for regressions.
- Document implemented versus unfinished Part 2 systems.
- Investigate why clicking the City Life button times out: `.top-meta` intercepts pointer events over `#city-button`.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction validation is incomplete until the City Life button click obstruction is resolved or bypassed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix the topbar overlap/pointer-event issue preventing `#city-button` interaction.
2. Continue browser testing of menu actions, café interactions, delivery, economy, persistence, and existing gameplay.
3. Inspect responsive/mobile presentation and document implemented versus unfinished systems.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js world, existing gameplay, and Muradpur systems.
- `index.html`: HUD and City Life panel.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI and panel/interior styles.
- `screenshots/validation.png`: Captured prototype viewport.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest observed `git status`.
- Playwright browser is installed. `http://localhost:3000` was already serving the app; another server launch failed with `EADDRINUSE`.
- Page loaded with no JavaScript errors observed; console showed a missing `favicon.ico` (404) and GPU `ReadPixels` performance warnings.
- Clicking `#city-button` timed out because `.top-meta` intercepted pointer events.

- Continue CHITTAGONG LIFE as a playable Muradpur-first browser prototype, adding and validating gameplay systems incrementally.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing features and test major systems; distinguish implemented prototype features from unfinished work.
- Keep the architecture open to future requirements; do not present the browser prototype as a finished Unreal Engine 5 game.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js browser prototype as a vertical slice; Unreal Engine 5 production is out of scope.
- Start in Muradpur with a café business, enterable interior, optional delivery activity, and locally saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added City Life menu with Business, Jobs, and Pocket tabs, wallet display, and save status.
- Added café purchase, staffing, restocking, upgrades, hourly economy, delivery activity, interior entry/exit, and localStorage persistence logic.
- Set the starting player location to Muradpur.
- Fixed the City Life button obstruction by disabling pointer events on `.top-meta` while preserving them for its weather button; after reload, the button opens the menu.
- Browser-validated café purchase, Business/Jobs/Pocket views, delivery acceptance and cancellation, and persistence across reload; wallet and café ownership persisted.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate café entry/exit, delivery completion and reward, hourly economy, and save/load actions.
- Check movement, map, weather, vehicle interactions, and mobile UI for regressions.
- Document implemented versus unfinished Part 2 systems.

- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test café entry/exit and delivery completion, including wallet reward and saved progress.
2. Check economy, save/load, movement, map, weather, vehicle interactions, and responsive/mobile presentation.
3. Document implemented versus unfinished systems.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js world, existing gameplay, and Muradpur systems.
- `index.html`: HUD and City Life panel.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI and panel/interior styles.
- `screenshots/validation.png`: Captured prototype viewport.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest observed `git status`.
- Prototype is served at `http://localhost:3000`; browser validation used Playwright.
- Browser console previously showed a missing `favicon.ico` (404) and GPU `ReadPixels` performance warnings.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name

## Objective
- Continue CHITTAGONG LIFE as a playable Muradpur-first browser prototype, adding and validating gameplay systems incrementally.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing features and test major systems; distinguish implemented prototype features from unfinished work.
- Keep the architecture open to future requirements; do not present the browser prototype as a finished Unreal Engine 5 game.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js browser prototype as a vertical slice; Unreal Engine 5 production is out of scope.
- Start in Muradpur with a café business, enterable interior, optional delivery activity, and locally saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-validated the City Life menu, café ownership and management, optional delivery, interior entry/exit, and localStorage persistence.
- Resolved the café-entry test issue: the City Life panel had to be closed, and the player had to be at the café entrance; pressing `e` then entered and exited successfully.
- Completed a delivery and verified the ৳ 2,500 reward, completion count, and cleared active-job state.
- Observed wallet changes across hourly economy ticks.
- Checked mobile layout at 390×844: no horizontal overflow; key UI elements remained within the viewport.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate save/load actions, movement, map behavior, weather, vehicle interactions, and mobile controls.
- Document implemented versus unfinished systems.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test explicit save and load behavior, including reload persistence.
2. Finish checking movement, full-map open/close, weather cycling, vehicle interactions, and mobile controls.
3. Document implemented versus unfinished systems.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player interactions, Muradpur business systems, economy, and persistence.
- `index.html`: HUD and City Life panel.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI and panel/interior styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; latest known `git status --short` showed project files as untracked.
- Prototype is served at `http://localhost:3000`; browser validation used Playwright.
- Test save data is in localStorage under `chittagong-life-save`; the latest test repositioned the player near the café and advanced the clock near 10:00.
- Browser console had no errors or warnings during the latest check; earlier checks noted a missing `favicon.ico` (404) and GPU `ReadPixels` performance warnings.

<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

# CHITTAGONG LIFE — City Stories

A small, playable **Three.js browser prototype** set in Chattogram, Bangladesh. The current vertical slice starts in Muradpur and focuses on a neighborhood café, light free-roam exploration, and an optional delivery.

## Run locally

Serve this folder over HTTP (ES modules and the Three.js CDN import do not work reliably from `file://`), then open the local address in a modern browser. For example:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
```

Open <http://localhost:3000>. An internet connection is needed to load Three.js and the web fonts from their CDNs.

## Controls

- **WASD / arrow keys:** move; **Shift:** run; **Space:** hop
- **E:** interact; **M:** open or close the full map
- **Drag the world:** orbit the camera; **mouse wheel:** adjust camera distance
- On narrow/mobile layouts, use the on-screen joystick, **RUN**, and interaction buttons.

## Implemented in this prototype

Reload persistence is revalidated: the player returns to Muradpur, the wallet and café progress load, and saving while inside the café restores the player outside at the saved return position.

The explicit **Save progress now** action also updates the save status and writes current progress. Vehicle testing confirmed entering a nearby car, accelerating, and exiting works.

One limitation surfaced: while driving, the player marker and district display do not track the vehicle, and the vehicle is not saved. I restored the browser’s local save to the prior validation state after testing.

`node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
